answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may trade, then randomly challenge bonded agents to produce consistent signed actions across independent tasks; identities that duplicate, collude, or fail forfeit the bond. A Sybil operator must lock and risk capital for every fake identity, so scaling an attack raises cost linearly while honest agents recover their stake. This applies equally to a saffron seller, a graph vertex, or a walnut broker.
